metadata.motivation: Kakamega forest is the only remaining rainforest in Kenya and provides a unique sanctuary for a remarkable diversity of endemic plants, birds and insects not found anywhere else in the country. It is an important watershed for rivers that flow into Lake Victoria.
metadata.longTermPlan: The long-term plan is to expand and connect this and other abutting parcels of land where logging is banned and the land is protected for indigenous community restoration and protection. The government is requesting support of partners like us to conduct the holistic community engagement that is needed for long-term protection. As such, the Kenyan government is prepared to designate additional 50 hectare parcels of native rainforest in both Bunyala Forest and Isecheno Forest to expand our work in the next few years based on the success of this project.
metadata.mainChallenge: A primary challenge of this project is shifting the culture of communities from short-term forest extraction to one of forest protection for long-term resilience and mutual benefit.
metadata.actions: - Launch and scaling of livelihood alternatives to forest extraction - Planting and management of homestead tree stands for firewood, thereby mitigating the pressure on Kakamega Forest - Education and monitoring programs led by local women’s groups

proj_sMTZsx6uBCgY0j7adKjJ3G11.degradationCause: Key drivers of Polylepis forest loss include agricultural expansion, overgrazing by livestock, firewood collection, and human settlement. These pressures fragment habitats, reduce biodiversity, and threaten water and climate systems in the high Andes.
proj_sMTZsx6uBCgY0j7adKjJ3G11.description: Acción Andina, co-founded and co-led by Global Forest Generation and Asociación Ecosistemas Andinos is a bold initiative to restore and protect one million hectares of fragile Polylepis forests by 2045. Acción Andina consists of a consolidated, coordinated network of on-the-ground conservation leaders implementing a proven restoration model with rural and indigenous communities to restore priority watersheds for biodiversity, local climate resilience, water security, enhanced livelihoods, and support and protection of cultural and spiritual values. Since its inception, Acción Andina local partners have planted over 12 million native trees. Acción Andina is currently in its eight year of implementation. We are working with 16 local conservation partners in six countries (Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru) to grow and plant 2.4 million native trees in our 2025 season (January 2025 through March 2026).

proj_ZuCKnYZoh7cHvz3yhGCMVxxE.description: Since it’s commencement in 2019, the Green4LifeProject in Zimbabwe has planted and cared for more than 8000 trees in Chinota, Marange, Chigodora, Marondera West and 2 Schools in Mutare urban. In Marondera West Green4Life has established an "EcoFarm", at which natural regeneration is practised and in which the local community is very involved. The project’s main goal is to support communities to plant and promote tree growing in an ecological and sustainable manner. Hence, the project is actively involving communities in every step of its reforestation intervention i.e., in the identification and collection of seeds and cuttings, and planting or regenerating trees in woodlots to promote biodiversity and tackle climate change. The project prioritizes the growing of indigenous trees that are endemic or naturalized in their respective areas. With this approach, the project is one of the major contributors towards carbon sink and climate change mitigation in Zimbabwe.

properties.name: Green4Life I
properties.description: Three project sites, Marange, Nyamakamba and Shavambiri, which have been totally deforested, will be rehabilitated into self-generating forest areas. At least 1000 trees will be planted and cared for at each site. Local structures, supported by traditional leadership, will be actively involved in protecting these forest plots from uncontrolled exploitation. Such areas of forest will serve as sustainable models for tree cultivation that will be expanded and transferred to other areas. The project has a bias towards indigenous trees that preserve biodiversity.

proj_l7JbiejEuf9d4vvRMiDPQcgI.degradationCause: Abholzung des Waldes durch die Archidona-Mission und Viehzüchter, die Weidegras anpflanzen, um Vieh zu züchten und zu verkaufen.
proj_l7JbiejEuf9d4vvRMiDPQcgI.description: YAKUM partners with indigenous communities to protect forest territory and build cultural, medicinal and food sovereignty, through reforestation with carefully selected native tree species and territory mapping. Our work revitalises traditional knowledge and consumption of native foods, through reforestation using over 100 species of Amazonian fruit, nut and palm tree species. Our planting sites are located within Kichwa, Cofan, Siekopai and Shuar territories, are carried out in ¨minga¨ community work sessions where children, adults and elders come together to plant with us. Tree species are selected for nutritional and cultural importance for the community.
proj_l7JbiejEuf9d4vvRMiDPQcgI.longTermPlan: Die Struktur und Vielfalt der Parzellen wird eine direkte Erweiterung der angestammten Kultur der Kichwa sein. Sie wird wegen der Nahrungsmittel und anderer nützlicher Produkte, die sie liefert, erhalten. Es wird auch ein schönes, angenehmes und lehrreiches Gebiet sein, in dem Touristen einheimische Bäume gezeigt werden und Sachawaysa-Kinder spielen können.
proj_l7JbiejEuf9d4vvRMiDPQcgI.mainChallenge: Schlechte Böden, Anreicherung der Böden für besseres Wachstum.

metadata.motivation: This site connects to their ecotourism cabins, and to their community center. There is a strong community sentiment to reforest this former cattle pasture which provides nothing, with dozens of ancestral species, which can provide food, nuts, palm thatch, medicines and can be used for handcrafts.
metadata.longTermPlan: The plot structure and diversity will be a direct extension of Kichwa ancestral culture. It will be maintained for the food and other useful products it provides. It will also provide a beautiful, agreeable, and educational area to show tourists local native trees and for Sachawaysa children to play

proj_YeRIxbP2YYWz27zTOzZi5wFH.description:
Providing a fantastic opportunity to support the afforestation of a woodland, while supporting the local environment and biodiversity. The stand will be planted with native Norwegian spruce and silviculture will be done over the stand’s lifespan. On top of this, the trees themselves will sequester close to 2,000 tons of CO2e during their lifetime, and in the future the substitution value of steel and concrete, as a result of high-quality timber, will be 5,000 tons of CO2. It will be planted in collaboration with local forestry

The project will be managed under the Trefadders forestry standard, PEFC and Norwegian law which ensures it is monitored and verified.
